title: Region capacity + drain plan (us-east ⇄ eu-west) — failover readiness sheet
content:
Last updated: 2026-02-05 (Vanessa)

Purpose
- Provide a single place to answer: “Can we safely fail over Hosted API + Dedicated from us-east to eu-west (and reverse) without cascading overload?”
- Defines baseline load, usable headroom, drain rates, and hard ‘safe to failover’ criteria.
- This sheet is used for game day go/no-go and for on-call decisioning during real regional impairment.

Scope / notes
- Regions covered: us-east (primary), eu-west (secondary) for Game Day #1 scenario; reverse direction noted for follow-up.
- Workloads:
  - Hosted API (shared pools; multi-tenant)
  - Dedicated (reserved pools; tenant-specific)
- Capacity figures are “effective capacity” (after reserving for N+1, maintenance, and guardrails). Do NOT treat raw GPU counts as available.
- Units:
  - RPS = requests/sec at gateway
  - TPS = tokens/sec at runtime (aggregate output tokens/sec)
  - p95/p99 = tail latency as seen by client
- Assumptions (for planning, not a contract): model mix is dominated by 2–3 large decoder models + embeddings; worst-case is long context + streaming.

================================================================================
A) Baseline load and capacity summary (rolling weekday peak, last 14 days)
================================================================================

Table A1 — Hosted API shared pools (all tenants)
(peak hour averages, plus 5-min max in parentheses)

Region | Effective GPU capacity (normalized) | Peak gateway RPS | Peak runtime TPS | Avg GPU util | p95 latency | p99 latency | Notes
us-east | 1.00 (reference) | 1,420 (1,760) | 2.95M (3.40M) | 62% | 820ms | 1.9s | Primary for NA traffic; higher long-context share

Summary of us-east effective pool makeup (for intuition only; not exhaustive)
- “Large gen” pool: ~60% of effective capacity
- “Mid gen” pool: ~25%
- Embeddings/rerank: ~15%

Region | Effective GPU capacity (normalized vs us-east) | Peak gateway RPS | Peak runtime TPS | Avg GPU util | p95 latency | p99 latency | Notes
eu-west | 0.82 | 690 (910) | 1.55M (1.95M) | 58% | 910ms | 2.2s | Higher cross-region client latency for NA; lower long-context share

Important: eu-west has lower effective capacity today due to (a) fewer large-gen nodes, (b) more frequent maintenance windows, (c) stricter batch caps for latency.

Table A2 — Dedicated reserved pools (top tenants likely to be in blast radius)
(‘steady’ is typical weekday; ‘peak’ is 95th percentile hour)

Tenant / Tier | Home region | DR region | Reserved effective capacity | Steady util | Peak util | Notes / constraints
Atlas Payments (Enterprise, Dedicated) | us-east | eu-west | 0.06 (of us-east reference) | 41% | 71% | Requires auditability of any flips; no >2 policy flips/hr
Northstar Health (Regulated, Dedicated) | us-east | eu-west | 0.04 | 36% | 55% | Data residency: EU-only for certain workloads (see security guidance); confirm before any cross-region
2 other mid-size Dedicated (anonymized) | us-east | eu-west | 0.05 total | 33% | 62% | Can tolerate brief brownout during drain if pre-notified

Dedicated notes
- Dedicated failover is not “free”: DR region pools must have warm capacity and compatible model artifacts preloaded.
- For the controlled test, blast radius should be limited to: Hosted API canary routes + 1–2 Dedicated tenants explicitly opted in.

================================================================================
B) Headroom calculation + ‘safe to failover’ criteria
================================================================================

Definitions
- Usable headroom = (effective capacity) - (current load) - (reserve buffers)
- Reserve buffers are mandatory:
  - N+1 / maintenance: 10% of effective capacity (hard)
  - Incident jitter buffer (avoids stampede + retries): 10% (hard)
  - Dedicated isolation buffer in DR: varies by tenant (see below)

Table B1 — Hosted API headroom snapshot thresholds (must be true for GO)

Signal (target region receiving traffic) | GO threshold | NO-GO threshold | Source
Large-gen GPU util (5-min avg) | ≤ 65% | ≥ 75% | fleet/gpu utilization
Queue depth / scheduler backlog | < 1.5s equivalent | > 3.0s | runtime scheduler metrics
p95 latency burn (multi-region view) | < 1x SLO burn | > 2x SLO burn sustained 5m | SLO burn dashboards
5xx error rate (gateway) | < 0.3% | > 1.0% sustained 2m | gateway + SLO
Retry rate (client-visible 429/503) | stable or decreasing | increasing trend for 10m | gateway overload metrics
Cross-region reachability probes | green (no packet loss, stable RTT) | flapping/red | perf-canary probes

Operational “math” (rule of thumb)
- To fail over 100% of us-east Hosted API traffic into eu-west, eu-west must have:
  - ≥ 45% usable headroom (large-gen pool) at time of action
  - AND queue depth must remain < 1.5s equivalent under 10% traffic ramp test
- Rationale: during impairment, retries + timeouts can inflate load by 15–30% for ~5–10 minutes if circuit breakers aren’t already shedding.

Table B2 — Dedicated DR readiness criteria (per tenant)

Criterion | GO | NO-GO | Notes
DR pool warm | model artifacts present + warmed cache OR prewarm completed | cold artifacts or missing model version | warm defined as: first token < 1.5x baseline during preflight
DR isolation buffer | ≥ 20% free within tenant pool | < 10% free | avoids tenant self-overload during switch
Routing policy limits | within per-tenant flip budget | would exceed budget | see per-tenant safety limits (policy engine)
Customer comms | opt-in confirmed (for planned tests) | no confirmation | for real incidents, follow comms playbook

================================================================================
C) Drain & evacuation rates (how fast we can shift safely)
================================================================================

Drain “rate” here is traffic shift rate + node drain rate. Both must be respected.

Table C1 — Hosted API traffic shift ramp (policy weights)

Step | Action | Max delta | Hold time | Validation query (must pass)
1 | Start canary shift to DR | +5% traffic to DR | 10 min | DR p95 < +15%; DR 5xx < 0.5%; queue depth < 1.5s
2 | Ramp | +10% increments | 10 min each | same as above; plus watch retry-after and 429 trend
3 | Ramp | +20% increments | 15 min each | queue depth stable; no SLO burn >2x
4 | Full failover (if required) | to 100% | 15 min | no cascading overload; us-east continues to shed/limit

Hard stop / rollback triggers during ramp
- DR queue depth > 3.0s equivalent for > 2 minutes
- DR 5xx > 1.0% for > 2 minutes (excluding known client cancels)
- DR p99 > 4.5s sustained 5m AND burn rate > 2x
- Any evidence of policy oscillation (more than 2 flips in 30m)

Table C2 — GPU node drain rates (infra operations)

Pool type | Node drain method | Safe drain concurrency | Expected drain per node | Notes
Hosted shared | cordon + drain (no new placements) + runtime graceful stop | 5% of nodes per 10 minutes | 8–15 min depending on in-flight | do not drain >10%/20m unless DR headroom is massive
Dedicated | per-tenant drain endpoint/workflow | 1 tenant at a time by default | 10–25 min per pool | coordinate with routing; ensure audit events emitted

Key gotcha: draining nodes increases tail latency briefly as batching efficiency drops. Don’t combine aggressive drain with aggressive traffic shift.

================================================================================
D) “Safe to failover” checklist (GO/NO-GO) — use for game day + real events
================================================================================

Preflight (T-60 to T-15)
- [ ] Confirm target region (DR) meets Table B1 thresholds for 30 minutes leading up to planned shift.
- [ ] Confirm cross-region probes are green (reachability + RTT stable), and DNS/anycast changes are not in progress.
- [ ] Confirm gateway circuit breaker configs are current (timeouts/retry budgets) and overload responses (retry-after) enabled.
- [ ] Confirm no ongoing maintenance in DR region (fleet, networking, control plane).
- [ ] Confirm DR has sufficient unreserved capacity (or Dedicated DR pools are explicitly warm).

Go/No-Go criteria (hard)
- GO only if:
  - DR large-gen util ≤ 65% (5-min avg) and queue depth < 1.5s equivalent
  - DR 5xx < 0.3% and not trending upward
  - Reachability probes green
  - On-call + Infra lead explicitly acknowledge stop conditions + rollback owner is assigned
- NO-GO if any:
  - DR util ≥ 75% or queue depth > 3.0s equivalent
  - DR is already burning SLO (>2x) for any reason
  - Probe flapping or known network event
  - Control plane instability (policy engine, region health) — we don’t shift during controller uncertainty

During failover (T0 to T+30)
- [ ] Shift in steps (Table C1). Do not skip hold times unless us-east is hard down.
- [ ] Watch for thundering herd: retries rising, connection churn, streaming reconnect spikes.
- [ ] If overload: prefer shedding/429+retry-after to keep system stable; avoid flapping weights.

Post-failover stabilization (T+30 to T+120)
- [ ] Confirm DR steady-state util ≤ 70% (we need room for subsequent incidents)
- [ ] Confirm Dedicated tenants in scope are stable (p95 + error) and audit log complete
- [ ] Document exact times of shifts and any manual interventions (for SLO + postmortem)

================================================================================
E) Directional notes: eu-west → us-east (reverse failover)
================================================================================

We can generally absorb eu-west into us-east faster than the opposite direction, but only off-peak in us-east.
- us-east is the heavier region; reverse failover can create “double peak” if done during NA business hours.
- Preferred reverse window for controlled tests: 02:00–05:00 ET.

Recommended reverse criteria
- us-east util ≤ 55% and queue depth < 1.0s equivalent for 30m before starting.
- Start with 10% → 25% → 50% increments (since us-east headroom is usually higher) but still hold 10–15m.

================================================================================
F) Risks / open questions (tracked for review)
================================================================================

Risks
- Metric lag / aggregation: if DR looks “green” but capacity signal is delayed, we can overshoot. (Mitigation: require corroboration from queue depth + probes.)
- Client retry amplification: some SDK defaults are too aggressive; can create transient 5xx spikes during redirect. (Mitigation: gateway retry-after + docs; streaming reconnect fix.)
- Dedicated surprise load: Dedicated tenants may run batch jobs unexpectedly. (Mitigation: tenant pool headroom check + optional pause window for planned tests.)

Open questions
- Should we increase eu-west large-gen effective capacity by +10–15% before enabling full automation? (Infra: possible but requires procurement/lead time.)
- Do we want a formal “max safe failover percentage” per hour for Hosted API (e.g., never shift >50% within 30m unless reachability is red)?

================================================================================
G) Quick links (where to look during an event)
================================================================================

- Failover signal dashboards: reachability, error burn, latency burn, capacity headroom, policy flips
- Runbook: GPU pool drain + evacuation procedure
- Runbook: Hosted API regional failover (on-call)
- Linear umbrella: ENG-2411
